outcome: cardiovascular events (cardiac failure/arrest, stroke, myocardial infarcts and other events)
cohort: The study included 223,502 singleton deliveries from the US Consortium on Safe Labor between 2002 and 2008.
finding: Exposure to nitric oxides and specific toxic air pollution species (ethylbenzene, m-xylene, o-xylene, p-xylene, and toluene) 5-6 days prior to delivery was associated with increased odds of cardiovascular events during labour/delivery, while ozone exposure showed decreased odds.
